headline: Calcutta HC: Cross-objection maintainable in Section 260A income tax appeals
reference: Principal Commissioner of Income Tax vs Birla Corporation Limited, ITA No. 124 of 2019 with OCO No. 19 of 2020, Calcutta High Court (Division Bench), 2026:CHC-OS:444-DB
summary_points: Issue: whether a respondent can file a cross-objection in a High Court appeal under Section 260A of the Income Tax Act, 1961.
Held: Section 260A(7) applies CPC provisions on appeals 'as far as may be', so Order XLI Rule 22 CPC applies and cross-objection is maintainable.
The Court disagreed with Smt. Jyoti Kumari (Karn) and Nagar Dairy (Del), and relied on Hari Shankar Rastogi and Bikram Singh (SC).
Limit: cross-objection must be confined to the adverse part of the Tribunal order and raise a substantial question of law.
Appeal listed on 30 November 2026 to formulate the respondent's substantial questions of law.
who_is_affected: Assessees and the Revenue who are respondents in Section 260A appeals before the High Court, and their advisers and counsel.
action_required: Respondents with adverse findings in the Tribunal order should consider filing cross-objections with a substantial question of law, keeping in mind that other High Courts have taken a contrary view.

Calcutta High Court on cross-objections in income tax appeals

In Principal Commissioner of Income Tax vs Birla Corporation Limited (14 October 2026), a Division Bench held that a respondent can file a cross-objection in an appeal under Section 260A of the Income Tax Act, 1961.

Key reasoning:
- Section 260A(7) applies CPC provisions on appeals to the High Court 'as far as may be'.
- Order XLI Rule 22 CPC is not inconsistent with Section 260A, so the right need not be spelt out expressly.
- The Court relied on Hari Shankar Rastogi and Bikram Singh (SC), and disagreed with the Karnataka High Court in Jyoti Kumari and the Delhi High Court in Nagar Dairy.

Important safeguard: the cross-objection must stay within the adverse part of the Tribunal's order and must raise a substantial question of law. It cannot widen the Court's jurisdiction to questions of fact.

The appeal is listed on 30 November 2026 to formulate the respondent's questions.

Please verify the details with the official judgment before relying on it.
